standard_prerequisites.name: A perfect complex on a quasi-compact scheme has bounded tor amplitude and its cohomology modules are of finite type
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 9800-9808 and again at proof lines 9820-9825
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the interval on which the induction runs and the finiteness used to build the surjection in the induction step.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finitely presented module of tor dimension zero is finite locally free
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the top cohomology in the base case with a finite locally free module.

standard_prerequisites.name: On a scheme with the resolution property the surjection onto a finite type module can be realized by a finite locally free module, and the kernel of such a surjection between finite locally free modules sits in an exact sequence controlled by the cone
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite locally free module and the distinguished triangle used to reduce the interval.

core_obligations: Choose integers a and b such that the complex has tor amplitude in the interval from a to b and vanishes below a, using that the object is perfect on a quasi-compact scheme; if b is smaller than a the complex is zero and there is nothing to prove (proof lines 9800-9806).

Argue by induction on the length b minus a, the assertion being the existence of a complex concentrated in degrees a to b with finite locally free terms and a quasi-isomorphism to the given complex (proof lines 9807-9811).

Base case: when b equals a, the top cohomology is the kernel of the differential out of degree b, which is a finitely presented module of tor dimension zero and hence finite locally free, so the complex reduces to that module placed in degree b (proof lines 9812-9818).

Induction step: the top cohomology is a finite type module, so after choosing a surjection onto it from a finite type module and lifting that map to the kernel of the differential, build a map from a finite locally free module onto the relevant part (proof lines 9819-9850).

Form the distinguished triangle with that map and the resulting cone, note that the cone has shorter tor amplitude interval, apply the induction hypothesis to it, and conclude that the original complex admits a bounded complex of finite locally free modules with a quasi-isomorphism to it (proof lines 9851-9887).
proof_roadmap: Bound the tor amplitude and set up the induction on the length of the interval (proof lines 9800-9811).
Base case: the interval has length zero and the top cohomology is finite locally free (proof lines 9812-9818).
Induction step: strip the top cohomology with a finite locally free module and a cone of shorter interval (proof lines 9819-9887).
